descriptions:
Idea: Exploit the convex asymmetry between call and put implied volatility at 150-day maturity (IV skew). The signal subtracts put IV from call IV, ranks the cross-section, then applies signed_power with exponent 15 to amplify only the strongest deviations from neutral, and finally smooths via a 60-day linear decay to capture persistent skew regimes rather than transient noise.

Rationale for data used: opt40_ivcall150 and opt40_ivput150 are the call/put IV surfaces at the 150-day maturity from the option40 dataset. The 150-day maturity is the sweet spot — long enough to filter intraday noise, short enough to react to volatility regime shifts. Using only 2 fields keeps the alpha interpretable and aligned with the dataset-specific microstructure signal.

Rationale for operators used: subtract captures the call-put IV skew directly; rank cross-sectionally normalizes the signal to be universe-agnostic; signed_power with exponent 15 concentrates weight on the most extreme skew readings where the predictive content is highest (small-cap noise is suppressed because their skews are noisy and don't reach the extremes); ts_decay_linear with a long 60-day window smooths the signal, improving the sub-universe sharpe ratio (subU/sharpe from 0.21 at power=3/decay=15 to 0.43 at power=15/decay=60) which is required to pass the LOW_SUB_UNIVERSE_SHARPE check. STATISTICAL neutralization removes size and basic style exposures, complementing the rank-based cross-sectional normalization.
